summary: CUDA-Q Logical is a retargetable compiler infrastructure that lowers logical programs through a logical virtual machine, QEC microcode, physical gate schedules and real-time control plans while preserving semantics and provenance. Resource estimates are derived directly from these compiler artifacts and reconcile with established independent models, including for qLDPC surgery.
motivation: Fault-tolerant toolchains are currently stitched together by hand, which separates resource estimates from the artifacts they describe and makes architecture comparisons unreliable.
method: A layered, extensible compiler in which QEC codes, execution models, decoders and hardware architectures are modular extensions and every layer verifies composition and resource constraints.
result: Schedule-derived estimates agree with independent models across application-architecture studies, qLDPC surgery and detector-error-model composition, and expose cost drivers hidden by aggregate formulas.
